title: Primitive parameter stewardship: conventions and upgrade sprint
body:
Purpose and scope:

This note captures conventions for parameter stewardship across our Terraform primitives (VPC, IAM, cluster primitives for EKS/GKE/AKS) and defines a practical upgrade sprint plan to change interfaces without creating widespread disruption. Intended audience: infra module owners, platform SREs, solutions engineers who onboard customers, and the release engineering team that coordinates module rollouts.

Why this matters (short):
- We repeatedly run into three classes of issues when evolving primitives: incompatible variable renames, surprising default changes, and poorly scoped outputs that break downstream stacks.
- For private deployments we must minimize customer blast radius and provide clear dovetailing for on-prem and cloud variants.
- A single source of variable/outputs conventions + a tested upgrade sprint reduces incident churn and manual migration work.

High-level stewardship conventions (opinionated):
1) Stable surface area: each primitive exposes a small, documented set of inputs considered stable. Anything outside this set is "advanced"/internal and flagged in docs.
2) Names: use explicit nouns and avoid provider-specific acronyms. Examples: vpc_cidr_block, subnet_private_cidrs, bastion_ssh_key_name. Avoid vpcCidr, private_subnet_cidrs.
3) Versioned inputs: prefer explicit versioned input groups when changing semantics (e.g., iam_bindings_v1 -> iam_bindings_v2) instead of mutating the shape in-place.
4) Defaults: defaults should be conservative and safe for production (no open security groups, no public ECR access). When changing defaults, follow the upgrade sprint (see below).
5) Outputs: outputs must be minimal and idempotent. Avoid exposing provider-specific IDs unless necessary; provide a stable alias output (e.g., cluster_endpoint, cluster_kubeconfig_ref) that the rest of the stack consumes.
6) Telemetry outputs: each module must emit (via outputs) a consistent set of telemetry-friendly attributes: module_name, module_version, region_hint, lifecycle (created/updated). These are for the console's inventory.

Module interface contract template (example):
- description: short one-liner of the primitive's responsibility
- inputs_stable: [list of input names that are part of the stable contract]
- inputs_advanced: [list of advanced/escape hatch inputs and a warning in docs]
- outputs_stable: [public outputs other modules should rely on]
- outputs_internal: [internal outputs for migration/debug only, mark deprecated when needed]
- compatibility_guarantees: semantic versioning blurb and what we promise between patch/minor/major bumps

Sample variable naming (concrete examples):
- vpc_name (string) - stable
- vpc_cidr_block (string) - stable
- subnet_private_cidrs (list(string)) - stable
- subnet_public_cidrs (list(string)) - advanced
- enable_nat_gateway (bool) - stable
- nat_gateway_spec (object) - advanced, provider-specific hints

Sample outputs (concrete):
- vpc_id (string) - stable alias
- subnet_ids_private (list(string)) - stable alias
- nat_gateway_ips (list(string)) - internal (avoid unless required)

Cross-cloud considerations: EKS / GKE / AKS primitives
- Keep cluster primitives surface aligned by creating a small common interface (cluster_name, node_pools, control_plane_endpoint) and provider specific extensions grouped under provider_node_pools or provider_control_plane.
- Avoid exposing provider resource ids directly; provide mapping outputs when necessary (e.g., aks_node_resource_group_name).
- For on-prem (airgapped) variants: include an image_registry_override input and wiring for customer-provided cert bundles. Treat these as stable for private deployments.

Upgrade sprint plan (4-week template) 
Goal: perform a safe, auditable module API change (rename or default change) with automated migration guidance and minimal customer action.
Week 0 - prep (2 weeks if large):
- Author the module-change RFC (small doc) and include: change summary, proposed new interface, backward compatibility story, migration tool plan, test matrix.
- Run quick static scan across internal repos to find consumers of existing inputs/outputs (simple grep + dependency map).
- Create a compatibility shim inside the module: accept old input names and map to new ones while emitting a deprecation output and a terraform plan-time warning via null_resource/local-exec (see caveats).

Week 1 - canary & testbeds:
- Publish a release candidate (x.y.z-rc1) and tag modules in the internal registry.
- Roll the RC into internal testbeds (infra bootstrap, QA clusters, two small customer sandboxes) and run the full terraform plan/apply suite.
- Validate telemetry outputs and console inventory shows expected attributes.
- Collect breakage candidates and update migration scripts.

Week 2 - incremental rollout:
- Promote to GA minor release with deprecation grace period documented.
- Run mass static replacement jobs for internal stacks (codemod + PR generation) for obvious literal uses. Manually triage edge cases.
- Notify customer success and solutions engineering of the rollout with a clear migration guide and a migration PR template they can apply.

Week 3 - cleanup and deprecation tracking:
- After a 30–60 day grace, remove internal shim that mapped old inputs to new if no consumer projects remain or if they have migrated.
- Publish a deprecation report (who's using old inputs) and archive the RFC.

Compatibility patterns and technical mechanics:
- Shims: implement input shims inside the module that convert old shapes to new and set a boolean output deprecated_input_used = true. Avoid using provider-time warnings because terraform has limited runtime warning APIs; use documentation and plan-time messages when possible.
- Codemods: provide a repo-level sed/python codemod that can rewrite variable references and minimal tests to validate. Keep these small and idempotent.
- Import scripts: where resource renames change resource addresses, provide terraform state mv snippets as a scripted output to run from the consuming repo root.

Testing matrix (minimum):
- Plan only tests across multiple terraform versions we support.
- Apply tests in a disposable environment (CI using ephemeral accounts) for: basic create, update without changing stable inputs, major change path with both old and new inputs present (shim active).
- Golden outputs: run a small harness that asserts outputs_stable exist and are stable across upgrades.

Risk matrix (quick):
- Breaking rename (high): requires codemods + state moves. Mitigation: long deprecation period, state-move automation, single-PR mass migration for internal customers.
- Default change (medium): silent behavior changes. Mitigation: convert default -> no default and require explicit opt-in via new flag; use canary testbeds.
- Output removal (high): downstream stacks break. Mitigation: keep outputs with a deprecation tag for at least one minor release, add alias outputs.

Sprint task checklist (example items to assign):
- RFC authored and reviewed (owner: Priya).
- Static consumer scan and dependency map produced (owner: Marcus).
- Shim implemented and unit tested (owner: Jamal).
- RC published to internal registry (owner: Release Eng).
- Codemod script + repo PR generator (owner: Elena).
- Run codemod across internal repos and open PRs (owner: infra automation).
- Customer comms + migration guide published (owner: Solutions Eng).
- GA promotion and deprecation tracking dashboard entry (owner: Product Ops).

Operational notes and gotchas:
- Terraform plan-time warnings: we can't inject true plan warnings; therefore include a local-exec that echoes a clearly prefixed message during create/update. Keep this removable and gated behind a variable to avoid noisy output in CI.
- State drift risk: avoid changing addresses quietly. If you must change resource addresses, include a clear state mv section in the release notes and test it in a script.
- Provider differences: cloud providers have different limits (subnet counts, route table semantics). Document these in the primitive's README and add preflight checks where possible (data lookup + assert).

Example migration snippet (documentation-only, not executed):
- Rename variable my_old_subnets -> subnet_private_cidrs
1) Add shim variable my_old_subnets (type = list(string), optional) and map: subnet_private_cidrs = coalesce(var.subnet_private_cidrs, var.my_old_subnets)
2) Output deprecated_input_used = length(var.my_old_subnets) > 0 ? true : false
3) In codemod: replace var.my_old_subnets with var.subnet_private_cidrs in consuming repos and open PRs.
4) After 60 days, remove shim and bump major if needed.

Appendix: recommended module checklist for PR review (pre-merge):
- Are inputs grouped and documented into stable vs advanced?
- Are new defaults safe for production?
- Is there a shim or migration path for any renamed input/output?
- Are outputs minimal and aliased when provider-specific?
- Do unit tests exist to validate mapping/shim behavior?
- Have internal consumers been scanned and notified?
- Is there a deprecation timeline included in the changelog?

Next steps (practical):
- Run the dependency scan for the three most active internal modules this week and identify the top-5 breaking candidates.
- Pick a single small rename + shim and exercise the full 4-week plan as a dry run in January sprint.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Add a short terraform module template repository with shim examples and codemod utilities.
- Wire module telemetry outputs into the console inventory so we can report on deprecated_input_used across customers.
- Loop in Legal for any customer-facing migration notices where contract SLAs might be impacted.

End of doc.
